concepts.proposed_markdown:
### Custom-field key discovery and audit

Bearer-authenticated `POST /v1/customFields/listKeys` retrieves all "your" active custom-field key definitions and can filter by a supplied array of managed entity types. Organization, account, environment, permission, and caller-visibility scope are not defined, so completed traversal is not authority for an organization-wide inventory. HTTP `200` requires sibling `data` and nullable `next_page`; every result requires `entity`, `key`, and `enforce_uniqueness`, so the operation inventories definitions and their uniqueness setting rather than entity values or mutation outcomes. The body itself is not marked required, `entities` is not required within a supplied object, and unknown-property behavior is unspecified. The response uses the same 19-value `ManagedEntity` enum as key mutations, while the overview names a narrower eight-entity prose set; the sources do not reconcile that applicability boundary or labels such as `product` versus `contract_product`. Repeat each returned `next_page` until null for supported traversal. The endpoint schema documents no `limit`, while the API-wide pagination authority says all list endpoints expose `limit` and `next_page`, recommends `1` and `50`, and caps `limit` at `100`; whether `listKeys` accepts, rejects, or ignores `limit`, its default, applicability, and precedence are unresolved. Neither authority defines active-state timing, order, total count, cursor lifetime, stable snapshot, concurrent-change behavior, freshness, or read-after-mutation visibility. [[source-metronome-api-reference-custom-fields-list-custom-field-keys]] [[source-metronome-api-reference-pagination]]
warnings: Preserve the definition-inventory scope; do not claim organization-wide completeness, assigned values, or that uniqueness currently holds across entity instances.
Do not reconcile the 19-value ManagedEntity schema with the overview's narrower entity prose by inference.
Do not infer omitted-body or unknown-field runtime behavior from the open request schema.
Preserve the endpoint-versus-global limit contradiction; do not infer either endpoint rejection or definite applicability of the generic limit guidance.

For custom-field configuration audits, bearer-authenticated `POST /v1/customFields/listKeys` returns all "your" active key definitions, optionally filtered by managed entity type. Organization, account, environment, permission, and caller-visibility scope are not defined, so even completed cursor traversal does not establish organization-wide configuration coverage. HTTP `200` requires sibling `data` and nullable `next_page`, and each item requires entity, key, and uniqueness-setting fields. Repeat with each returned `next_page` until null. The endpoint schema documents no `limit`, while the API-wide pagination authority says all list endpoints expose `limit` and `next_page`, recommends `1` and `50`, and caps `limit` at `100`; `listKeys` acceptance, rejection, default, applicability, and precedence remain unresolved. Neither authority defines order, total count, cursor lifetime, snapshot consistency, duplicate-or-skip behavior during concurrent key changes, as-of marker, freshness guarantee, or read-after-create/remove visibility. The inventory also contains no assigned entity values or duplicate-value counts, so it cannot by itself prove value coverage, uniqueness compliance, export completeness, invoice propagation, or external-system reconciliation. [[source-metronome-api-reference-custom-fields-list-custom-field-keys]] [[source-metronome-api-reference-pagination]]
warnings: Treat the endpoint as caller-visible configuration discovery, not an organization-wide audit or a complete entity-value or reconciliation report.
Complete cursor traversal does not establish a stable point-in-time inventory while key definitions change.
Preserve the endpoint-versus-global limit contradiction and unknown applicability.

concepts.proposed_markdown: - [[source-metronome-api-reference-custom-fields-list-custom-field-keys]] - custom-field definition audit within unresolved caller-visible scope, entity filtering, top-level cursor placement, endpoint-versus-global limit contradiction, and ordering, snapshot, freshness, value-coverage, and reconciliation boundaries

`POST /v1/customFields/listKeys` is a paginated configuration read under the separate API-wide `Idempotency-Key` authority. After execution admission, identical same-key parameters replay the persisted original result rather than prove a fresh active-key view or new stable pagination snapshot. Advancing query `next_page` or changing the body `entities` filter changes request parameters, so reusing that key then returns HTTP `409` under the API-wide contract. The endpoint does not require the header, prescribe key use across pages, or add local cursor lifetime, cache freshness, concurrent-change, read-after-mutation, another-key, expired-key, or recovery behavior. [[source-metronome-api-reference-custom-fields-list-custom-field-keys]] [[source-metronome-api-reference-idempotency]]
warnings: Keep the execution-admission and changed-parameter behavior sourced to the separate API-wide idempotency authority.
Do not treat replay as a fresh configuration audit or infer a preferred key-per-page policy.
